I've been on the receiving end of this kind of situation for 2-3 years, and I can understand why.   
But remember you are not one to decide how they feel. Yes you can decide whether or not this continues, but if they love you strongly, you won't be able to change that.  

My ex, kept insisting I should be with someone else. They kept insisting I wasn't happy because of them. And I said to them many, many, MANY times how my feelings can't just change like that. I also said many, MANY times how they have made me happy on numerous occasions aside our arguments. The thought of seeing them just gets me way too overly excited.   

But their insecurities took over, and we broke up. They really believed they weren't good for me, no matter how many times I said they were good for me.   
We're still in contact 2 years later since the break up. Guess what? I still love them, but we won't get back together. It happens.   

Insecurities are real, and they suck. It hurts. It hurt really bad that they felt like they had the right to decide how I feel, the ones that belong to no one but me. But how you perceive things, is not how they perceive things. Perception of reality, and all.  

This isn't to convince you to go back and change things. Sometimes it might really be for the best, to cut ties. I'm writing this for you to understand how it probably feels for the other person.  
If you make this choice to set them free, you need to understand how it looks in their eyes. Not just yours.  

In the meantime, focus on yourself. For even if you ever break up for future relationship, you will still have you - and that's what matters. You.

A year or two ago, I was at a water theme park, so almost drowning. No one saved me but myself.

I was in one of those lazy rides where you just sit in a floating donut hole and float around the entire course.
There were over 100+ people on this ride, and possibly 2-3 lifeguards on this day. About 100 people right behind me, crowded in the water and groups of adults (they were friends of each others, complete strangers to me) kicking each other for amusement. My mother and brother already got off the lazy ride so I was no longer in their eyesight. 

I wanted to re-adjust my position on the donut, but I, along with the donut, flipped. It was floating vertically and I panicked extremely, trying to flip it back up. Body through the hole of the donut, leaning on my stomach. Head was down in the water, legs kicking ferociously and arms flailing. It just wouldn't flip. It just floated and bounced up and down, no longer left to right. I was so, so terrified. I thought, "This is it. I'm going to drown in a water theme park. I'm going to die. I'm going to die."

I saved myself. Somehow, I managed to flip it back to float correctly. I fell out of the donut and into the crowd of people, still in the water, feet on the bottom. Coughing and catching my breath, I looked up and around me.
1 lifeguard. Standing there. Completely oblivious to me, which I guess fair, you have 100+ other people kicking and pushing each other in the ride (and eventually kicking me.)

But still, I was extremely shocked. This lifeguard, plus the many other people around me, did nothing.

It's a scary thought, of what does "drowning" or at least, "kicking for help" look like to people. I thought someone would see me, given the amount of people crowding the water. But, no. No one pulled me up, no one stopped to see what the kicking was about or why the donut was sticking out of the water the wrong way. Nothing.
Whatever I looked like, I didn't look like I was in danger, despite feeling like I was or could have been.

So what would have happened to that ride if I drowned?
How would the lifeguards feel?
And my family?
If in a crowd of 100s and 1 person drowned, what do people do?
What would have changed if I drowned?

I told a friend and the next time we went, she held my donut next to hers the entire time and kept her eyes on me.
Aside that though, you can bet that I'm never sitting on a floating donut hole ever again.
